title: Counit object is terminal in the right-slice pullback of a homotopy-2-category adjunction
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, degreewise pullbacks, right-pinched mapping spaces and contractibility of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the right slice $\mathcal C_{/t}$ over a vertex with its source projection of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Let $\mathscr K$ be a simplicial category (simplicial hom-sets, identity vertices, strictly associative unital simplicial composition) whose every hom-simplicial set is a quasicategory. Its homotopy $2$-category has the same objects, hom-categories the homotopy categories of these quasicategories, and composition induced by that of $\mathscr K$. Let $L\in\mathscr K(c,d)_0$ and $U\in\mathscr K(d,c)_0$, and let $\eta:1_c\to UL$ be an edge of $\mathscr K(c,c)$ and $\epsilon:LU\to1_d$ an edge of $\mathscr K(d,d)$ whose classes form an adjunction $L\dashv U$ in the homotopy $2$-category: writing whiskering as composition in $\mathscr K$ with a degenerate edge, $[\epsilon L]\circ[L\eta]=[1_L]$ in the homotopy category of $\mathscr K(c,d)$ and $[U\epsilon]\circ[\eta U]=[1_U]$ in that of $\mathscr K(d,c)$.

Fix an object $z$ and a vertex $a\in\mathscr K(z,d)$. Put $C_z=\mathscr K(z,c)$ and $D_z=\mathscr K(z,d)$, let $L_z:C_z\to D_z$ be the simplicial map of composition with $L$, let $q_a:(D_z)_{/a}\to D_z$ be the source projection of the right slice over $a$, and form the degreewise pullback
$$E'_z=C_z\times_{L_z,D_z,q_a}(D_z)_{/a}.$$
Its vertices are pairs $(b,\alpha)$ with $b\in C_z$ and $\alpha:L_zb\to a$ an edge of $D_z$. Let $Ua\in C_z$ be the composite of $a$ and $U$, and $\epsilon_a:LUa\to a$ the edge of $D_z$ obtained by composing $\epsilon$ with the degenerate edge at $a$; thus $(Ua,\epsilon_a)$ is a vertex of $E'_z$. Then $E'_z$ is a quasicategory and $(Ua,\epsilon_a)$ is terminal in it: for every vertex $(b,\alpha)$ of $E'_z$ the right-pinched mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_{E'_z}((b,\alpha),(Ua,\epsilon_a))$ is contractible.

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Observation 4.3.4 and Theorems 4.3.9 and 4.3.11, pp. 840--844 (terminality of the counit in the slice over a); right slice as in Kerodon 018F/01KX. Online source read; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The two displayed triangle equalities are equalities of edge classes in the homotopy categories of the quasicategorical hom-simplicial sets. By the edge homotopy quotient calculus, choose 2-simplex witnesses whose successive edges are L eta and epsilon L with long edge 1_L, and eta U and U epsilon with long edge 1_U. Strict simplicial composition in the simplicial category curries each such 2-simplex to a coherent triangle homotopy in the corresponding functor simplicial set: for every z, whiskering gives coherent functors L_z:C_z to D_z and U_z:D_z to C_z, transformations eta_z and epsilon_z, and homotopies epsilon_z L_z composed with L_z eta_z approximately 1 and U_z epsilon_z composed with eta_z U_z approximately 1. This construction uses the actual simplicial composition maps, so it retains all higher simplices and does not infer coherence from component classes alone.

source.place: Observation 4.3.4 and Theorem 4.3.9, coherent triangle witnesses; here the witnesses are obtained directly by the homotopy-category edge quotient and strict simplicial whiskering.

proof.text: The source projection q_a:(D_z)_{/a}\to D_z is a right fibration by the slice theorem, hence has all inner-horn lifting properties. Pulling its lifting squares back along L_z shows that E\prime_z\to C_z is a right fibration. Since C_z is a quasicategory, the same fillers show that E\prime_z is a quasicategory. This argument is degreewise and also covers an empty pullback. The vertex (Ua,epsilon_a) is present because q_a(epsilon_a)=LUa=L_z(Ua).

source.place: Right-slice construction and right-fibration projection (Kerodon 018F/01KX), specialized to K=Delta^0; the pullback horn argument is the degreewise base-change calculation.

proof.text: Fix a vertex (b,alpha) of E\prime_z and abbreviate P=Map_{C_z}(b,Ua), M=Map_{D_z}(L_z b,LUa), and S=Map_{(D_z)_{/a}}(alpha,epsilon_a). Because E\prime_z is a degreewise pullback, an n-simplex of its right-pinched mapping space is exactly a pair of n-simplices in P and S with equal image in M; thus Map_{E\prime_z}((b,alpha),(Ua,epsilon_a)) is the strict pullback P\times_M S. The map S\to M induced by q_a is a Kan fibration: q_a is an inner fibration by Step 2, so this is precisely the relative mapping-space assertion of the inner-mapping-fiber lemma. Therefore the strict pullback agrees, via the Kan pullback/path comparison, with the homotopy pullback P\times^h_M S, retaining all higher path data. The mapping spaces P, M and S are Kan by the mapping-space clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], taking the functor shape to be Delta^0.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.1 (relative right-pinched mapping-space Kan fibration), together with Kerodon 018F/01KX for the right-slice mapping spaces.

proof.text: Put $T_a=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D_z)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D_z}\{a\}$, with source projection $t_a$. The slice-arrow comparison supplies a functor equivalence $\delta_a:(D_z)_{/a}\to T_a$ with $t_a\delta_a=q_a$. Its degree-zero formula has $\rho_0:\Delta^0\times\Delta^1\cong\Delta^1$, so it sends the vertices $\alpha$ and $\epsilon_a$ to those very arrows in $T_a$. Write $R=\operatorname{Map}_{T_a}(\alpha,\epsilon_a)$. The assertion that every functor equivalence induces equivalences on mapping spaces in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes the actual induced map $j:S\to R$ a weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. Moreover $j$ is strictly over $M$: applying the right-pinched mapping construction to $t_a\delta_a=q_a$ gives $t_{a,*}j=q_{a,*}$. This is the required comparison on mapping spaces, rather than an inference from the slice equivalence alone.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.4.20 and Construction 4.6.4.15; mapping-space preservation is the cited enhanced-functor calculus statement.

proof.text: Set $N=\operatorname{Map}_{D_z}(L_zb,a)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-comma-mapping-pullback] with $\mathcal C=\mathcal D=D_z$, $F=\mathrm{id}_{D_z}$, $\mathcal B=\Delta^0$, and $G(*)=a$. Its comma category is exactly $T_a$, and its two chosen objects are $(L_zb,*,\alpha)$ and $(LUa,*,\epsilon_a)$. It gives $R\simeq M\times^h_N\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^0}(*,*)$, with the first projection the actual $t_{a,*}$. The right-hand mapping space has exactly one simplex in every degree, directly from its definition. The first map to $N$ is $u:h\mapsto\epsilon_a\circ h$; the second is the vertex $1_a\circ\alpha$. These are canonical mapping-space compositions of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Its unit homotopy gives a specified path $1_a\circ\alpha\simeq\alpha$. Apply the homotopy-commuting pullback-invariance lemma with identity equivalences on $M$, $\Delta^0$ and $N$, constant homotopy on $u$, and that unit homotopy on the other leg. Thus $R\simeq H:=M\times^h_N\{\alpha\}$ over $M$; the comparison keeps the $M$ coordinate and concatenates the path with the unit homotopy. No equality of composition with a chosen strict representative is assumed.

source.place: Composition, unitality and pre/postcomposition in Subsection 4.6.8; the general comma formula and homotopy-commuting comparison are agent-formulated in the cited existing nodes.

proof.text: Let $\ell:P\to M$ be the actual map on mapping spaces induced by $L_z$. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] first to the strictly commuting cospan comparison $(\mathrm{id}_P,j,\mathrm{id}_M)$. It gives $P\times^h_M S\simeq P\times^h_M R$. Apply the same lemma to the equivalence $R\simeq H$ of Step 5 over $M$, keeping $P$ and $M$ fixed. If this equivalence is represented by a zigzag, apply it to each leg; for an over-$M$ comparison specified up to homotopy use [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-commuting-pullback-invariance] with that specified homotopy. Thus Step 3 gives $\operatorname{Map}_{E'_z}((b,\alpha),(Ua,\epsilon_a))\simeq K:=P\times^h_M H$. In the diagram with top row $K\to H\to\{\alpha\}$ and bottom row $P\xrightarrow{\ell}M\xrightarrow{u}N$, both adjacent squares are homotopy pullbacks by their path-space definitions. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], including its specified-homotopy clause: the outer square is a homotopy pullback, with its path obtained by concatenating the two square paths. Consequently $K\simeq P\times^h_N\{\alpha\}$, where the map from $P$ is exactly $f=u\ell$, namely $h_0\mapsto\epsilon_a\circ L_z(h_0)$. All inputs are Kan complexes and all replacements preserve the displayed projection or its specified homotopy.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.1.11 (pasting), Proposition 3.4.0.9 (032B, invariance), and the cited specified-homotopy extension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-adjunction-mapping-equivalence] to $F=L_z$, $G=U_z$, $x=b$, $d=a$, and the coherent unit, counit and triangle homotopies constructed in Step 1. It states that $N\to P$, $v\mapsto U_z(v)\circ\eta_b$, is an equivalence, with inverse homotopy class represented by $h_0\mapsto\epsilon_a\circ L_z(h_0)$. With the canonical composition of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], this latter map is the map $f=u\ell$ of Step 6, so $f:P\to N$ is an equivalence of spaces. In particular the argument concerns all simplices of the mapping Kan complexes, rather than only the adjunction bijection on components.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.1.17 and the dual counit formula of the cited adjunction-mapping-equivalence statement.

proof.text: The vertex $\alpha:L_zb\to a$ is a vertex of the Kan complex $N$. By [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence], the homotopy fiber $P\times^h_N\{\alpha\}$ of the equivalence $f$ of Step 7 is contractible. Step 6 identifies this fiber up to weak homotopy equivalence with the right-pinched mapping space into $(Ua,\epsilon_a)$ from $(b,\alpha)$. Its map to a point therefore induces a bijection on components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups, since the same is true of the fiber and of each comparison equivalence. This is precisely contractibility as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Since $(b,\alpha)$ was arbitrary and $E'_z$ is a quasicategory by Step 2, this is the stated terminality of $(Ua,\epsilon_a)$.

source.place: Remark 3.4.0.6: every homotopy fiber of an equivalence of Kan complexes is contractible; terminality uses the stated mapping-space definition.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 2, derived mapping-complex adjunction before the inverse limit; coherent unit/counit data and the Riehl--Verity slice argument are expanded here.

lean.note: Mathlib SimplicialCategory supplies strict simplicial composition and its homEquiv identifies ordinary morphisms with all vertices. The helper triangle predicate uses equality in Mathlib homotopy categories.
